items.title: ICE and Hyperliquid Partnership
points: Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged double-digits after Intercontinental Exchange (ICE, the NYSE's parent company) announced a deal to bring regulated perpetual futures (leveraged derivative contracts that never expire) based on Hyperliquid to the U.S. market.
ICE will become the exclusive operator of regulated markets for Trade[XYZ], which runs real-world asset markets on Hyperliquid, and is taking a strategic stake in the company.
The regulated perpetual futures markets still require regulatory approval with no announced launch date.
Investor Stan Druckenmiller, who backs Trade[XYZ], expressed interest in using the product, while ICE CEO Jeffrey Sprecher clarified it is additive to existing futures markets, not a replacement.

items.title: Bitcoin Options Expiration and Rate Outlook
points: $11 billion in Bitcoin options expire Friday on Deribit—about one-third of all its Bitcoin options—creating potential market volatility.
The Federal Reserve held rates steady Thursday, but two officials voted to hike rates in December.
Hot PCE inflation data (Personal Consumption Expenditures, a key U.S. inflation gauge) published Thursday lifted market expectations of a December rate hike to 83% probability, per Reuters.

items.title: Regulatory Actions Against Crypto Platforms
points: Utah filed felony charges against prediction market platform Kalshi and its co-founders, claiming an undercover agent placed a dozen sports wagers on the platform.
The CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the U.S. derivatives regulator) sued Utah one day later to block the state's enforcement actions against Kalshi.
Justin Sun's HTX exchange settled with the UK Financial Conduct Authority, agreeing to stop targeting UK consumers—marking the regulator's first enforcement case against a crypto firm over marketing.

items.title: Bitcoin and Gold Price Dynamics
points: Bitcoin trades near $80,762, down 2.5% over the past month, with both BTC and gold falling together after hot PCE inflation data.
Bitcoin's price sits about halfway between prediction-market targets of 10 and 30 ounces of gold per BTC (currently around 20 ounces).
57% of Myriad prediction market traders lean toward Bitcoin eventually being worth only 10 ounces of gold, implying BTC would need to lose half its value relative to gold.
Gold fell 1.1% Thursday following the hot PCE data.

items.title: Treasury Sanctions North Korean IT Worker Scheme
points: U.S. Treasury sanctioned 11 individuals tied to a North Korean IT worker scheme that moved millions of dollars in crypto.

items.title: Franklin Templeton Bitcoin ETFs Launch
points: Franklin Templeton launched two new Bitcoin ETFs (Exchange-Traded Funds, investment funds traded on stock exchanges like regular shares) on Nasdaq, expanding institutional access to cryptocurrency trading.
The launch is seen as a major institutional adoption milestone as an established financial services firm enters the crypto space.

items.title: Dubai Royal Family $1.5B Bitcoin and Property Strategy
points: A Dubai royal-backed firm unveiled a $1.5 billion strategy combining Bitcoin holdings with real estate investments.
The move signals a wealth diversification trend among major international investors blending cryptocurrency with traditional property holdings.
